phase3_findings.description: 'ls -l prints minute granularity' is a false universal: entries older than roughly six months print a year form with no time field, which is precisely the stale-leftover case the comparison exists to catch.

Step 1's routing sentence promises the read-only fallback for any write under .prflow/tmp/, but that file declares a closed per-artifact set with no generic arm; several .prflow/tmp writes have no arm and one routes to a different file. A refused mkdir also fell outside the 'write under' predicate.

A path appearing in neither a listing row nor a diagnostic fell through every classification arm, which is the ordinary result when a runner surfaces stdout and drops stderr. 'Present' and 'never observed' collapsed onto the same behaviour, so nothing re-entered and nothing reported.

The fallback reference's opening paragraph declares every arm per-artifact and enumerates by name the arms that write and delete nothing of their own; the arm this change adds is cross-artifact and absent from that enumeration, falsifying its own file's header.

The listing shown in the draft-rendering message is taken before the producing-step re-entry, so on exactly the runs where the feature fires the user sees a superseded not-found line with no instruction to disclose that the listing predates the re-entry.

The invocation obliged the run to display error lines but nothing made diagnostics part of what it classified on; 2>&1 closes that at the source. Safe here because create-issue is local-tier only and no cloud workflow dispatches it.
The changeset's third sentence stated re-entry unconditionally while three arms in the same change re-enter nothing.

'discharge this listing' named the wrong object: paragraph 1 orders the listing unconditionally, so the read-only arm discharges the re-entry, not the listing. 'revision round' was also vocabulary the skill defines nowhere.

Prose weight on an always-loaded skill root, with several clauses pre-empting a reviewer misreading rather than instructing the agent. Measurement established the block at 498 words against a roughly 150-word target; compressed to 364, with the declined cuts each tied to a criterion or a previously closed Critical.

A Step 3.6 re-entry ordered by this block bypasses the audit lifecycle owner and can spend an audit round the presentation gate, which owns the same artifact under a different predicate, would not have spent.

fix_decisions.evidence: the issue's own scope forbids stating the Presentation-gate relation in the shipped file, so closing this here would contradict the specification the run is implementing

parking_evidence.basis: the finding is real but its remedy is barred by the issue's stated scope; it belongs in a follow-up that can revise that scope
parking_evidence.failing_input: a run whose audit artifact is absent or older than the run-slug pointer while the presentation gate would have accepted an inline stand-in

notes: The word-count figures reported in iterations 1 and 2 before this record (311, 302) were estimates presented as measurements; the subagent flagged its own error and the corrected trajectory was re-measured with the command recorded above.
Ten of the eleven acceptance criteria were re-read out of the rewritten block; AC11 was confirmed structurally, the block occupying lines 269-299 and the reference-load line 300.
